Simulation study - model 4

In this file a simulation study is conducted. The predicted values per method (ols - ridge regression -local shrinkage) are computed per simulated data set. The predicted values are then compared with the true values , known by design.
```{r}
library(glmnet)
library(Hmisc)
library(ggplot2)
library(MASS)
library(tidyr)
getHdata(gusto)
gusto.dat <- gusto

set.seed(4176340)


gusto.dat <- gusto[which(gusto$grpl %in% c(1,2,4) & gusto$grps %in% c(5,9,10,11)),] 
n_pat <- nrow(gusto.dat)  
gusto.dat$pat.id <- 1:n_pat

#V_1 is log-normally distributed
gusto.dat$V_1 <- rlnorm(
  n = nrow(gusto.dat),
  meanlog = log(gusto.dat$sysbp),
  sdlog = 0.5)

#V_2 is exponentially distributed:
gusto.dat$V_2 <- rexp(
  n = nrow(gusto.dat),
  rate= 1/gusto.dat$sysbp)

gusto.dat$SYS <- gusto.dat$sysbp
gusto.dat$AGE <- gusto.dat$age
gusto.dat$PUL <- gusto.dat$pulse
```



Functions for local shrinkage:

1- Cross validation to find the optimal threshold
```{r}
Cross_val_local_shrik <- function(neff, newdata,fold_k) { 
  
  mse <- rep(0,5)
  
  for(i in 1:5){
    train <- newdata[fold_k != i, ] 
    test  <- newdata[fold_k == i, ]
  
    
    #train set
    form1 <- y_sim ~ AGE + V_1 + V_2+ PUL 
    
    mod_OLS_base <- lm(formula = form1, data = train)
    
    X_ols <- model.matrix( ~ AGE + V_1 + V_2+ PUL , data= train)  
    XTX <- t(X_ols)%*%X_ols
    
    relvar_OLS <- numeric(length = nrow(X_ols)) 
    for(v in 1:length(relvar_OLS)){
      relvar_OLS[v] <- (t(X_ols[v,])%*%solve(XTX)%*%X_ols[v,])}
    
    #initialization
    
    Z_ols      <- X_ols[,-1] 
    n          <- nrow(Z_ols) 
    Z_shrink   <- Z_ols    
    relvar_it  <- relvar_OLS 
    z_bar      <- colMeans(Z_shrink) 
    zc         <- t(apply(X=Z_shrink, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x-z_bar})) 
    
    X_shrink   <- cbind(icpt=rep(1,n), Z_shrink) 
    iter       <- 0 
    maxiter    <- 1000
    dist       <- n*relvar_it - 1  
    diststart  <- dist  
    max_dist <- n*1/neff-1 
    
  
 
    Cov <- ginv(t(X_shrink)%*%X_shrink) 
    
    #loop while
    while(max(dist) > max_dist & iter < maxiter){ #while loop until all distances are below the threshold
  
  # compute the shrunk distance
      distshrink  <- dist
      distshrink[which(dist>max_dist)] <- max_dist #if dist > max_dist , dist is shrunk
  
  # compute shrinkage factor
      a           <- sqrt(distshrink/dist)
  
  
      azc         <- a*zc #shrink of the centered covariates
      Z_shrink    <- t(apply(X=azc, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x + z_bar})) #adding the mean 
  
      iter <- iter + 1  
      X_shrink   <- cbind(icpt=rep(1,n), Z_shrink)  #adding the intercept to the shrunk predictors
   
      z_bar      <- colMeans(Z_shrink) #calculating the mean of the shrunk covariates
  
      zc         <- t(apply(X=Z_shrink, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x-z_bar})) #recenter adding the mean computed after covariates shrinkage
  
  
      Cov        <- ginv(t(X_shrink)%*%X_shrink) #recompute the inverse of shrunk XTX
  
      relvar_it  <- diag(X_shrink %*% Cov %*% t(X_shrink))  
  
      n_eff      <- 1/relvar_it #recompute the effective sample size
  
      dist       <- n*relvar_it - 1  #recompute the distance
      }

  train_shrunk <- data.frame("y_sim" = train$y_sim) 
  train_shrunk <- cbind(train_shrunk, Z_shrink)
  mod_train_shrink <- lm(formula = form1, data = train_shrunk )
  
  #test set:
  X_ols_test <- model.matrix(~ AGE + V_1 + V_2+ PUL , data= test)
  
  relvar_OLS_test <- numeric(length = nrow(X_ols_test))  
  
  for(k in 1:length(relvar_OLS_test)){
    relvar_OLS_test[k] <- (t(X_ols_test[k,])%*%Cov%*%X_ols_test[k,])}
  
  n.test <- nrow(X_ols_test)
  test_distance <- n*relvar_OLS_test-1 #test set distances
  
  # shrink test set
  distshrink_test <- pmin(test_distance, max_dist)
  a_test <-  sqrt(distshrink_test / test_distance)
  
  
  Z_ols_test   <- X_ols_test[,-1] 
  
  Z_shrink_test <- Z_ols_test 
  relvar_it_test <- relvar_OLS_test

  zc_test        <- t(apply(X=Z_shrink_test, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x-z_bar})) #center the covariates of the test set
  azc_test <-zc_test*a_test #shrinking the test set covariates 
  Z_shrink_test    <- t(apply(X=azc_test, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x + z_bar})) #adding the mean 
  X_shrink_test <- cbind(icpt=rep(1,n.test), Z_shrink_test) 
  
  #compute MSE
  test_shrunk <- data.frame("y_sim" = test$y_sim) 
  
  test_shrunk <- cbind(test_shrunk, Z_shrink_test)

  dim(Z_shrink)
  pred <- predict(mod_train_shrink, newdata = test_shrunk)

  
  mse[i] <-  mean((test$y_sim- pred)^2)}

  mse_i <- mean(mse) #mean MSE
  
  return(mse_i)
}


```


2- Local shrinkage function for prediction in simulated data
```{r} 
local_shrik <- function(neff, newdata) { #function(threshold,data set)
  
    form1 <- y_sim ~ AGE + V_1 + V_2+ PUL  #model
    
    mod_OLS_base <- lm(formula = form1, data = newdata) #linear regression
    
    X_ols <- model.matrix( ~ AGE + V_1 + V_2+ PUL , data= newdata)  
    XTX <- t(X_ols)%*%X_ols
    
    #computing the inverse of the effective sample size per each subject in the sample
    relvar_OLS <- numeric(length = nrow(X_ols))
    for(j in 1:length(relvar_OLS)){
      relvar_OLS[j] <- (t(X_ols[j,])%*%solve(XTX)%*%X_ols[j,])}
    
    #initialization of local shrinkage algorithm
    Z_ols      <- X_ols[,-1] 
    n          <- nrow(Z_ols) 
    Z_shrink   <- Z_ols    
    relvar_it  <- relvar_OLS 
    z_bar      <- colMeans(Z_shrink) 
    zc         <- t(apply(X=Z_shrink, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x-z_bar})) 
    
    X_shrink   <- cbind(icpt=rep(1,n), Z_shrink) 
    iter       <- 0 
    maxiter    <- 1000
    dist       <- n*relvar_it - 1  
    diststart  <- dist  
    max_dist <- n*1/neff-1 

    Cov <- ginv(t(X_shrink)%*%X_shrink) 
    
    
    #while loop:
    while(max(dist) > max_dist & iter < maxiter){ #while loop until all distances are below the threshold
  
  # compute the shrunk distance
      distshrink  <- dist
      distshrink[which(dist>max_dist)] <- max_dist #if dist > max_dist , dist is shrunk
  
  # compute shrinkage factor
      a           <- sqrt(distshrink/dist)
  
  
      azc         <- a*zc  #shrinkage of the centered covariates
      Z_shrink    <- t(apply(X=azc, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x + z_bar})) #adding the mean 
  
      iter <- iter + 1  

      X_shrink   <- cbind(icpt=rep(1,n), Z_shrink)  #adding the intercept to the shrunk predictors
   
      z_bar      <- colMeans(Z_shrink) # calculating the mean of the shrunk covariates
  
      zc         <- t(apply(X=Z_shrink, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x-z_bar})) #re-center adding the mean computed after covariates shrinkage
  
  
      Cov        <- ginv(t(X_shrink)%*%X_shrink) #recompute the shrunk XTX
  
      relvar_it  <- diag(X_shrink %*% Cov %*% t(X_shrink))  #recompute  the inverse of XTX 
  
      n_eff      <- 1/relvar_it #recompute the effective sample size per subject in the sample
  
      dist       <- n*relvar_it - 1  #recompute the distance
      }


  newdata_shrunk <- data.frame("y_sim" = newdata$y_sim) 
  newdata_shrunk <- cbind(newdata_shrunk, Z_shrink)
  
  mod_newdata_shrink <- lm(formula = form1, data = newdata_shrunk ) #fitting the model on shrunk covariates
  
  pred_localS <- mod_newdata_shrink$fitted.values #fitted values
  
  return(pred_localS)
  
}
```

Simulation: true model
```{r}
#variables considered in the model
gusto.dat$SYS <- gusto.dat$sysbp
gusto.dat$AGE <- gusto.dat$age
gusto.dat$PUL <- gusto.dat$pulse



#true data
lm_original <- lm(SYS ~ AGE + V_1 + V_2 + PUL  , data = gusto.dat) #true model
summary(lm_original)

mu_i <- lm_original$fitted.values #true values

sigma <- summary(lm_original)$sigma

N_sim <- 100


#Empty matrix
pred_sim_ols <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(gusto.dat), ncol = N_sim)

pred_sim_ridge <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(gusto.dat), ncol = N_sim)

pred_sim_localS <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(gusto.dat), ncol = N_sim)

opti_neff_sim <- numeric(N_sim)
  
opti_lambda_ridge <- numeric(N_sim)


fold_k5 <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out= nrow(gusto.dat)))  #setting index per fold for 5-fold CV
```

Data generation
```{r}
y_sim_all <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(gusto.dat), ncol = N_sim) #empty matrix to save all the simulated variables

for (alpha_i in 1:N_sim) { 

  #simulated response variable y_sim:
  y_sim = mu_i + rnorm(n= nrow(gusto.dat), mean = 0, sd=sigma ) 
  
  newdata <- gusto.dat
  
  y_sim_all[, alpha_i] <- y_sim}


```

for loop linear regression
```{r}
for (alpha_ols in 1:N_sim) {
  
 
  newdata <- gusto.dat
  newdata$y_sim <- y_sim_all[, alpha_ols]
  
  # fit linear regression
  lm_sim_OLS <- lm(
    y_sim ~ AGE + V_1 + V_2 + PUL,
    data = newdata
  )
  
  # fitted values per simulation
  pred_sim_OLS <- lm_sim_OLS$fitted.values
  
  #saving fitted values
  pred_sim_ols[, alpha_ols] <- pred_sim_OLS
}
```

for loop ridge regression
```{r}
for (alpha_ridge in 1:N_sim) {
  newdata <- gusto.dat

  newdata$y_sim <- y_sim_all[, alpha_ridge]
  

  
  x = as.matrix(newdata[, c('V_1', 'V_2', 'AGE', 'PUL')]) #predictor matrix
  
  cv_ridge <- cv.glmnet(x= x,y= newdata$y_sim, alpha=0, lambda = c(1, 0.5,0.1,0.05,0.02,0.01, 0),foldid = fold_k5) #cv for lambda
  
  lambda_i <- cv_ridge$lambda.min
  
  opti_lambda_ridge[alpha_ridge] <-lambda_i
  
  lm_sim_RIDGE <- glmnet(x=x , y= newdata$y_sim , alpha = 0, lambda = lambda_i) #fitted model on newdata, chosen lambda
  
  pred_ridge <- predict(lm_sim_RIDGE, newx = x) #predict per each simulation
  
  pred_sim_ridge[,alpha_ridge] <- as.vector(pred_ridge)
  
}
dim(pred_sim_ridge)
```


for loop local shrinkage

To load the CSV file that already contains the local shrinkage predictions (previously calculated and saved in the file 'Simulation_Model_4_pred.csv'), read this file on the next chunk and skip the following code until the RESULTS section:
```{r}
data <- read.csv(
  "Simulation_Model_4_pred.csv",
  header = FALSE
)

data_local <- t(data)
dim(data_local)

pred_fileLocal <- as.data.frame(data_local)
```
Otherwise you can create the file from scratch and run the code below

creation of a file csv to save the predictions:

from column 1 to 20 
```{r}
for (alpha_local in 1:20) {
  newdata <- gusto.dat
  newdata$y_sim <- y_sim_all[, alpha_local]
  
  grid_neff <- c(0,50,120,150)
 
  mse_grid <- sapply(grid_neff, function(n) Cross_val_local_shrik(neff = n, newdata = newdata, fold_k=fold_k5))
  
  outp <- data.frame(neff =grid_neff,MSE = mse_grid)
  
  optimal_neff <- outp[which.min(outp$MSE), "neff" ]  

  opti_neff_sim[alpha_local] <- optimal_neff
  
  
  shrink_algo <-local_shrik(neff = optimal_neff , newdata = newdata)
  
  
  pred_sim_localS[,alpha_local] <- shrink_algo


  ############################
  row <- t(shrink_algo)    
  rownames(row) <- alpha_local  
  write.table(               #file creation
    row,
    file = 'test_model_4.csv',
    sep = ",",
    row.names = FALSE,
    col.names = FALSE,
    append = (alpha_local != 1)
  )
  #############################
}
```

  "test_model_4.csv",

RESULTS


MSE model 4
```{r}
#computing MSE per method as difference between predicted and true value
MSE_OLS <- colMeans(
  (pred_sim_ols- mu_i)^2
)

MSE_RIDGE <- colMeans(
  (pred_sim_ridge- mu_i)^2
)

MSE_LOCAL <- colMeans(
  (pred_fileLocal - mu_i)^2
)


mse_all <- cbind(OLS = MSE_OLS, Ridge =MSE_RIDGE, Local = MSE_LOCAL)


mse_min <- apply(mse_all, 1, min) #find minimum MSE between methods (per simulation)

best_method <- apply(mse_all, 1, which.min) 

best_method <- colnames(mse_all)[best_method]


results <- data.frame(
  z = 1:100,
  mse_min = mse_min,
  best_method = best_method
)

counts <- table(results$best_method) #counting the times each method achieves the lowest MSE

ratios <- counts/100
ratios
```

bias and variance:
```{r}
pred_meanLocal= rowMeans(pred_fileLocal)
ols_rowmean_sim <- rowMeans(pred_sim_ols)
ridge_rowmean_sim <- rowMeans(pred_sim_ridge)


bias_ridge =ridge_rowmean_sim- mu_i
bias_ols=   ols_rowmean_sim- mu_i
bias_local= pred_meanLocal- mu_i

#computing prediction variance per subject (across simulations):
var_ols <- apply(pred_sim_ols, 1, var) 
var_ridge<- apply(pred_sim_ridge, 1, var)
var_local <- apply(pred_fileLocal,1  ,var)

```

```{r}
median(bias_local)
median(bias_ols)
median(bias_ridge)

median(var_local)
median(var_ols)
median(var_ridge)
```

Bias distributions visualization through boxplots: 
```{r}
df_bias_wide <- data.frame(OLS = bias_ols, Ridge= bias_ridge, Local_Shrinkage=bias_local)


df_bias_long <- pivot_longer(
  df_bias_wide,
  cols = everything(),
  names_to = "method",
  values_to = "bias"
)

ggplot(df_bias_long, aes(x =method , y =bias , fill =method )) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "Method", y = "Bias distribution", fill = "Method", title = "Bias per subject - Model 4") +
  theme_bw()

```
